questions.q: What does the "D" in DAG stand for, and what does it mean?
options: Directed — every dependency arrow points one way, not both
Delayed — every task waits a fixed amount of time
Distributed — tasks run on many machines at once
Default — DAGs use default settings unless overridden
questions.explain: Directed means each edge has a direction: one task must finish before the next starts, never the reverse.

questions.q: Why does Airflow refuse to load a DAG file that contains a cycle?
options: If task A depends on B and B depends back on A, there is no valid order in which either could ever start
Cycles are allowed but run twice as slow
It's purely a style convention with no technical reason
Cycles are fine as long as there are fewer than three tasks
questions.explain: A cycle creates a circular wait with no valid starting point, so the schedule becomes uncomputable — it's a hard requirement, not a preference.

questions.q: In Airflow's Graph view, what does one box (node) represent, and what does one connecting line (edge) represent?
options: A node is one task; an edge is one dependency between two tasks
A node is one DAG run; an edge is a failure
A node is a Python file; an edge is an import statement
A node is a user; an edge is a permission
questions.explain: The Graph view renders the DAG's actual structure: tasks as nodes, dependencies as the edges connecting them.

questions.q: In the DAG code snippet from this lesson, what does `extract >> load` express?
options: An edge: the extract task must finish before the load task starts
A comment that Airflow ignores
That extract and load run at exactly the same time
That load must finish before extract starts
questions.explain: The `>>` bitshift operator sets a dependency — the task on the left must complete before the task on the right begins.

questions.q: If two tasks in a Graph view are drawn side by side with no edge connecting them, what does that indicate?
options: Neither task depends on the other — they can run in parallel
The DAG is broken and needs to be fixed
One of the tasks has been deleted
They are actually the same task shown twice
questions.explain: No edge between two tasks means there's no ordering dependency between them, so Airflow can run them at the same time.
